reading.body:
Banking is where AI governance predates the AI boom by more than a decade: Fed SR 11-7 model risk rules already cover credit and AML models, and generative AI in service and compliance is the new supervised frontier.

The pattern is that banking's AI oversight is older than the current generative wave. Credit and AML models have operated under SR 11-7 since 2011, so the sector enters the generative era with pre-existing validation, documentation, and model risk requirements. Treasury's report frames the supervisory conversation, and the Evident AI Banking Index provides a public scoreboard across talent, innovation, leadership, and transparency.

For AI specifically, this means generative deployments in service and compliance inherit a governance burden that most other industries lack. A bank cannot launch a customer-facing chatbot or compliance assistant without treating it as a model under SR 11-7, which slows deployment but also reduces the chance of unmanaged failures. The data does not show scale. It contains no figures on compute demand or power consumption for banking AI, and no adoption rates or model sizes. Governance is the constraint the data documents, not infrastructure.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey puts AI use in finance and insurance, NAICS 52, at 41.0% of firms in the latest reading, up from 36.5% in the prior period. The survey question asks whether the business used AI in the last two weeks, and the first time it was asked was September 2023. That makes banking and insurance one of the more measured adopters in the official data rather than a speculative one.

What the sector actually runs is not new. Fraud detection and credit models are decades old, and per this site's coverage, credit and anti-money-laundering models operate under the Federal Reserve's SR 11-7 model risk management guidance, issued in 2011. The Fed's supervisory letters index lists that letter, and the point the sources make is that banking is the sector where AI governance predates the AI boom by more than a decade. Generative AI in service and compliance is described as the new frontier, sitting on top of that older model risk regime rather than replacing it.

On the vendor and tooling side, this site's Financial Models section tracks the 1000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily, drawn from the Hub's public API and sorted by all-time downloads. The models are tuned for financial text, and the page states its tag provenance. Separately, the Evident AI Banking Index is described as the benchmark for the sector, scoring the major global banks across dozens of quantitative maturity metrics including talent, innovation, leadership, and transparency, and called the closest thing banking has to a public AI scoreboard.

The sources do not report ROI figures for banking AI, and no deployment cost or return numbers appear in the material provided. What they do report on the risk side is supervisory attention. Treasury's report on AI in financial services, covering uses, opportunities, and risks, is described as framing the US supervisory conversation. The excerpt drawn from the Treasury page itself concerns OFAC sanctions against a global gold smuggling and money laundering network, which speaks to the financial crime surface rather than to AI deployment directly.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material supports a narrow reading. Adoption is already substantial and rising in the official survey, the governance framework is not new, and any credit or AML model will be judged under SR 11-7 rather than under a fresh AI-specific rulebook. The public benchmarks that exist, the Evident index and the open model catalogue, measure maturity and availability rather than outcomes. Where the sources are silent, on ROI, on vendor pricing, and on sector-specific AI regulation beyond model risk guidance, there is nothing here to fill the gap.

https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-rel.brief: On International Anti-Corruption Day, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned 28 individuals and businesses tied to a Zimbabwe-based gold smuggling and money-laundering network led by Kamlesh Pattni. The Treasury says the scheme bribed officials, used trusted supporters to conceal ownership, and built a global web of companies to hide illicit activity, depriving Zimbabwe’s citizens of resource benefits while enriching corrupt officials and criminals. Acting Under Secretary Bradley T. Smith noted that “Corruption respects no borders” and that the action demonstrates a whole-of-government approach and collaboration with allies. The Treasury’s move is carried out under Executive Order 13818, which targets serious human-rights abuse and corruption worldwide. International Anti-Corruption Day, observed annually on December 9 since the 2003 UNCAC, aims to raise awareness of anti-corruption initiatives; the United Nations lists 189 parties to the convention.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisi.brief: This page lists the Federal Reserve Board of Governors’ 2011 supervision and regulation letters. It notes that a lock icon or https indicates a secure .gov connection and advises “Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.” It also contains guidance on prior notices concerning dividend declarations by savings association subsidiaries of savings and loan holding companies.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The page catalogues the 1000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub, listing each model's licence, download count and release date. It states the data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads and refreshed daily, with every model linking to its own Hub page. The page was last verified on 2026-10-04 and offers a citation format for the catalogue. It also notes that books by Stephen R. Jordan are available on Amazon, including a series titled "The Operating Discipline for AI Library", and that SRJ Consulting & Services has published a novel, The AI Lawyer, out 17 August 2026.
